_doc: HOW MUCH OF AN ACCOUNT'S PAST IS COPIED, AND HOW MUCH MEDIA STAYS ON THIS DISK (V2-936).
Measured on one real account before these numbers existed: the history walk had copied every Telegram
conversation back to 2020 — 168 000 messages, 16 MB of text, 93 MB of archive with its index (about 500 bytes
a message) — and 14 days of downloaded media were 1.9 GB in 1 329 files, one of them a 136 MB video. Text is
cheap and media is not, so each has its own bounds. A deployment that needs other values writes
`config/messaging.json` beside this file (same keys); 0 switches a bound off.
THE FIRST IMPORT (once per account, newest conversation first): a conversation is copied back `initial_days`
days or `initial_per_chat` messages, whichever comes first; at most `initial_chats` conversations; and the whole
import stops at `initial_messages`. 90 days holds the person who wrote two months ago; 150 conversations hold a
busy account's ~100 active ones with room; 300 a chat is weeks of a busy chat and the whole of a quiet one;
30 000 messages are about 15 MB on disk. A quiet account reaches the day bound first and copies little; a busy
one reaches the conversation and message bounds — the same numbers, spent newest first.
LIVE: every message that arrives or leaves is archived from the moment the account is linked, with no bound;
these numbers never apply to it.
ON DEMAND: a conversation somebody asks about (a search that names it, an errand) is copied `deep_messages`
further back per ask, whatever the first import left out, up to `deep_per_chat` in all.
MEDIA: a file over `media_file_mb` is never downloaded by itself (its type travels, the bytes stay at the
source); downloaded media is kept the days the operator chose and, whatever he chose, never more than the
SMALLER of `media_budget_mb` and `media_disk_ratio` of the disk that holds it — oldest file first out. On a
3 GB volume that is 450 MB; on a large disk the absolute cap rules.
A history the phone sends when a device is linked is trimmed to the same day and per-chat bounds.
